```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.4)
```

```{r setup}
library(quant2qual)
users <- mock_behavioral_data(300, include_truth = TRUE)
truth <- users$true_archetype
users$true_archetype <- NULL
```

The engine does three things, in order: **scale**, **band** and **match**. Each
choice is an argument, and each is recorded on the result so a report can state
exactly how a case was classified.

## Scale: relative to the cohort

A friction count of 6 means something different in a cohort whose median is 1
than in one whose median is 10. Every dimension is therefore standardised
against the cohort it came from. Three scalings are available:

| `scaling` | Centre | Spread | Use when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"z"` | mean | SD | distributions are roughly symmetric |
| `"robust"` | median | MAD (IQR/1.349 if the MAD is 0) | counts are skewed or have extreme cases |
| `"percentile"` | rank | normal scores of mid-rank percentiles | you want no distributional assumption |

`transform = "log1p"` is applied before scaling and suits durations and counts
with a long right tail.

```{r scaling}
fits <- lapply(c("z", "robust", "percentile"), function(s) {
  p <- identify_archetype(users, scaling = s)
  data.frame(scaling = s, agreement_with_truth = mean(p$archetype == truth),
             median_confidence = median(p$confidence))
})
do.call(rbind, fits)
```

## Band: low, mid and high

By default a dimension is *high* above `+threshold` and *low* below `-threshold`
on the standardised scale (`threshold = 0.5`). The threshold can differ by
dimension, and any dimension can instead use fixed **raw-unit cutpoints**: here
fewer than 2 errors is low friction and more than 8 is high, whatever the cohort
looks like.

```{r cutpoints}
p <- identify_archetype(users, threshold = c(velocity = 0.6, intensity = 0.6),
                        cutpoints = list(friction = c(2, 8)))
table(p$level_friction, cut(p$error_count, c(-Inf, 1.5, 8, Inf)))
```

The band edges are stored in raw units too, which is what the methods section
of a report quotes:

```{r edges}
sapply(attr(p, "q2q")$reference[c("velocity", "intensity", "friction")],
       function(r) round(r$edges_raw, 1))
```

## Match: rules, membership and confidence

An archetype is a set of allowed bands per dimension. The built-in UX matrix:

```{r matrix}
default_archetypes("ux")
```

Every case receives a **fuzzy membership** in every archetype. For each
constrained dimension, membership is a logistic ramp equal to 0.5 exactly on a
band edge and approaching 1 inside the allowed range (steepness `sharpness`);
the dimensions are combined by geometric mean. The fallback archetype's
membership is the membership of all three dimensions in the mid band.

```{r membership}
p <- identify_archetype(users)
archetype_membership(p[1:5, ])
```

Two assignment rules use these memberships:

* `method = "rules"` (default): the highest-priority archetype whose rule is met
  exactly, else the fallback -- a transparent `case_when()` cascade.
* `method = "fuzzy"`: the archetype with the highest membership.

`confidence` is the membership of the assigned archetype. A case near a band
edge gets a lower confidence and a named `runner_up`, and the narrative says so.

```{r borderline}
b <- select_cases(p, strategy = "borderline")[1]
generate_narrative(p, b, style = "brief")
```

## Defining your own archetypes

Rules accept single bands, adjacent combinations (`"low|mid"`,
`c("mid", "high")`, `"not_low"`) or `"any"`. Text fields may use `{subject}` and
`{Subject}`.

```{r custom}
m <- archetype_matrix(
  define_archetype(
    "Firefighter", velocity = "high", intensity = "high", friction = "high",
    theme = "crisis-mode working",
    persona = "A user fighting the product under time pressure.",
    interpretation = "{Subject} is working hard against repeated failure.",
    recommendations = c("Look for a single blocking defect on the critical path."),
    colour = "#C0504D"
  ),
  define_archetype(
    "Sprinter", velocity = "low", intensity = "high", friction = "not_high",
    theme = "fast, confident completion", colour = "#055F56"
  ),
  define_archetype("Everyone else", fallback = TRUE, theme = "unremarkable behavior")
)
m
custom <- identify_archetype(users, archetypes = m)
summary(custom)
```

## Checking a matrix against ground truth

With simulated data the planted signatures are known, so the matrix can be
validated before it is used on real data:

```{r truth}
table(simulated = truth, classified = p$archetype)
```

On real data, `plot_archetype_signatures()` and the borderline cases from
`select_cases(strategy = "borderline")` are the two most useful checks that the
rules describe groups that genuinely differ.
